messages:
sam: heads-up — ran the longctx perf harness this morning and saw steady mem growth on runtime nodes. looks like KV pages keep getting backfilled instead of evicted, hotset creeping. flame graph attached (perf://runs/5441122333/flame).

maria: link?

sam: perf://runs/5441122333/flame — pprof top shows 'kv_page_alloc' and 'kv_page_flip' at top. hotset growth ~2MB/s on the busiest GPU. sample: ```
# pprof top
30.2%  kv_page_alloc
18.7%  kv_page_flip
12.1%  kv_key_lookup
```

jonathan: is this new or regressed? what commit/shas involved?

sam: started after the kernel-selector change (PR #3421, sha: 6a1f9b2) which also adjusted our eviction ordering heuristics. can reproduce locally with longctx harness.

rita: did we change cache key construction recently? we trimmed prefix bytes in the key to save space last month. could be increasing collisions and causing unexpected reuse across sessions.

sam: here's the key builder snippet we use now: ```
// pseudo
key = hash(prefix[:64]) ^ session_id
if (trimmed) key = key & 0xffffffff
```
I suspect the truncation + xor with session_id creates aliasing between different prefixes when sessions rotate.

infra-bot: metric alert — kv.pageflip.rate increased 4x since 5441100000 for nodes in us-west-2. see dashboard /dash/kv-pageflip.

maria: can we test with session_stickiness=false? if reuse across sessions is the culprit toggling should reduce hotset. schedule a canary.

jonathan: also try adding tenant salt into the fingerprint (tenant_id || prefix fingerprint). cheap change, lowers collision probability. add metric for 'prefix_collision_count'.

sam: agreed. I'll run a canary with (a) session_stickiness=false, (b) fingerprint = sha1(tenant||prefix[:128]), and (c) revert the eviction ordering tweak.

rita: note: switching eviction from LRU->MRU for prefix pages might help because our longctx workloads re-access recent prefixes heavily. MRU avoids evicting the very pages that will be reused within the same request burst. but MRU can hurt multi-tenant mixing, so we should gate it behind a policy.

maria: watch out — our batching heuristics can make this worse. larger batches cause more aggressive prefix reuse inside a single batch, which amplifies hotpage residency. if you're running canary, run with both default and small-batch config so we can compare.

sam: plan: (1) run canary w/ session_stickiness off + tenant-salted fingerprint, two batch sizes; (2) collect kv.pageflip, prefix_collision_count, mem_growth rate; (3) temporarily revert PR #3421 eviction order if canary shows improvement. I'll kick off runs and post results.

jonathan: sounds good. thx sam. :thumbsup:

rita: optional: add a lightweight in-runtime metric that emits per-key fingerprint entropy histogram. will help detect truncation-induced aliasing early.

sam: adding that to the canary list. i'll update this thread with the first run logs / pprof link in ~2hrs.
